title: Types, Storage Classes, Scope & Linkage
desc: Fundamental types and their ranges, signed/unsigned conversion, storage classes (auto, static, extern, register), block/file scope, internal vs external linkage, and declaration vs definition.

title: Operators, Expressions & Sequence Points
desc: Operator precedence and associativity, implicit conversions and the usual arithmetic conversions, short-circuit evaluation, sequence points, and the undefined-behavior traps in ordinary expressions.

title: Control Flow & Program Structure
desc: if/switch/loops, fall-through, goto and labels, the comma operator, recursion and stack growth, and how source becomes control flow at the machine level.

title: Pointers Deep Dive
desc: Pointer arithmetic, pointer-to-pointer, arrays vs pointers, pointer to array vs array of pointers, const correctness, void* and generic code, and null/dangling/wild pointers.

title: Arrays, Strings & Memory Layout
desc: Array decay, multi-dimensional array layout, string literals and their storage, null termination, and hand-written string/array routines with real, compiled code.

title: Structures, Unions & Bit-Fields
desc: Padding and alignment, structure layout rules, unions and type punning, bit-fields and their portability limits, flexible array members, and packed structs for protocol parsing.

title: Type Qualifiers: const, volatile, restrict
desc: What const, volatile and restrict actually promise the compiler, volatile for hardware registers and signal handlers, and where each qualifier is misused.

title: Dynamic Memory Management
desc: malloc/calloc/realloc/free semantics, heap layout, alignment guarantees, memory leaks, double-free and use-after-free, and writing a simple custom allocator.

title: The Preprocessor & Macros
desc: Object-like and function-like macros, token pasting and stringizing, variadic macros, include guards vs pragma once, and the classic macro pitfalls (missing parens, multiple evaluation, statement-like macros).

title: Undefined Behavior & Standard Compliance
desc: Strict aliasing, signed integer overflow, out-of-bounds access, the difference between undefined, unspecified and implementation-defined behavior, and how the standard's wording actually reads.

title: Bit Manipulation & Numeric Representation
desc: Two's complement, endianness, floating-point representation basics, and the classic bit-twiddling interview questions (set/clear/toggle a bit, count set bits, power-of-two checks, swap without a temporary) with real code.

title: Function Pointers & C-Style Polymorphism
desc: Declaring and calling through function pointers, callback and dispatch tables, and emulating interfaces/polymorphism in C with structs of function pointers.

title: Compilation, Linking & the Build Pipeline
desc: Preprocessing, compiling, assembling and linking; translation units; object files and symbol resolution; static vs dynamic linking; and what a Makefile actually orchestrates.

title: Standard Library Internals
desc: stdio buffering and flushing, the string.h and ctype.h families, qsort/bsearch, and writing minimal versions of common library functions to show real understanding.

title: Core Data Structures & Algorithms in C
desc: Linked lists, stacks, queues, binary trees and hash tables implemented from scratch in C, plus the classic coding-round questions built on them (reverse a list, detect a cycle, and similar).

title: Debugging, Tooling & Sanitizers
desc: gdb workflows, Valgrind, AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, static analysis, and reading a crash or corruption back to its root cause.

title: Embedded, Firmware & Secure Coding in C
desc: Memory-mapped I/O, ISR-safe code and reentrancy, volatile hardware registers, buffer overflows and format-string bugs, integer-overflow-driven vulnerabilities, and the defensive-coding habits firmware review expects.

title: Principal-Level Systems Design in C
desc: Design questions with real code: a fixed-size memory pool allocator, a lock-free-ish single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer, a generic event/callback dispatch system, and how to reason about and present a C systems-design answer at the Principal level.
